title: George the Oak
subtitle: A beautiful tree that brings shade and reassuring blessing.

trails.title: Trail ① Bitter Medicine
trails.description: There is a notebook left in the drawer of the teacher's desk. The pale friends are also very interested in it.

content.text: Appendix to Foundation Potion Management Ⅱ

- Bitter Mute -

Warning: Appendix - Ⅱ Bitter Mute is an arcanum drug of Schedule Ⅱ. Arcanum Drug Possession License of the St. Pavlov Foundation is required for its possession. Organizations without the license must not produce or store the drug.
The drug is a concentrated solution for external use. When used, the solution should be diluted with pure water until the concentration reduces to the recommended range (45% - 65%). The concentration is adjustable depending on the condition (maximum safe concentration: 77%).

[Active ingredient] Screaming mandrake root, flying squirrel bile, toad liver (collected on full moon), two-headed snake tail scale powder, three-year-old belladonna (whole plant), leech.
[Caution] Use a copper cauldron for the production.
[Appearance & Property] A dark blue or dark brown concentrated solution with a pungent smell and an extremely bitter taste.
[Use] The drug can cause mental stability, and the bitter taste can cause temporary vision disorder and speech disorder. High concentrations can cause mild paralysis and even hallucination. Nowadays the drug's use in criminal penalty has been abolished and it is mainly equipped by the patrols and branches of the St. Pavlov Foundation. During daily patrols or under extreme circumstances mentioned by the Emergency Defense Code of St. Pavlov Foundation, the drug can be used as an effective suppression method against individuals or groups.

items.text: O Captain!
George the Oak
There is a huge, dark hole in the trunk of George the Oak. The hole connects to the ground, creating a natural fortress for animals.
This oak has been here for 700 years. It has witnessed each of the Parade Ceremonies.
Red squirrels and woodpeckers live in this hole all year round. Now, The Ring is kicking acorns inside. The clattering sound echoes in the huge hole.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Do you think they are gonna come?

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: What if, in the end, no one shows up ...

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: He paces in anxiety, kicking the acorns all over the place.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Maybe nobody cares what's outside the school; maybe everyone's happy with what they've learnt in the school ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At least there will be two ... I guess.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Isabella ...When she just got into the school, she was crying all the time and wanted to go home. Maybe she will come ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But this is something no one can guarantee.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... It'd be good enough as long as none of the instructors show up.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Vertin! Lo ... look outside ...!
Spots of light, just one or two of them, though dim as the fireflies, emerge in the dark.
Followed by many more of those.
Like stars in the night sky, the lights move quietly and slowly, merging into a Milky Way leading here.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: They are here ...! My God, that's ... Oh, and they—Everyone is here ...!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: How, how come there are so many of them!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Those are familiar faces—the silent ones during the day.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They're ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mesmer Jr., Isabella, "Penny," Matilda ... You are all here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Counting The Ring's classmates in, half of a class has gathered here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They jump into the tree hole one after another; the spacious hole suddenly becomes rather crowded.

items.speaker: All Students
items.text: After everyone has settled down with a place to sit or stand, there are sudden tensions in the air.

items.speaker: All Students
items.text: They look at each other. After all, this is a gathering that has been strictly prohibited and will be regarded as unethical and evil.

items.speaker: All Students
items.text: There is a long, breathtaking silence. Eventually, someone comes forward with a question.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Vertin ... You gathered us all here. Are you going to hold out against the principal?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What ...?!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Absolutely not! I've never thought of that!

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Phew ... That’s a relief.

items.speaker: Student B
items.text: I was so nervous. That was a harsh question you asked, Mesmer! But thank goodness ...

items.speaker: Student C
items.text: I'll be the first one out of here if it were a rebellion! This peace lover is not up against anyone!

items.speaker: Student C
items.text: Laughter from the crowd fills this narrow space.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Then what is it you want? We ... we came here in secrecy.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I didn't expect so many of you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So many of you in school are just like The Ring and me ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... want to know more about the things outside ...

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Those rumors ... Have you heard?

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Yet we are prohibited not only to say "that word," but also to speak about anything related to the outside world.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Our life is all about training, peace, and mankind. Nothing else.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We have different hair colors, speak with different accents, and cast different arcane skills ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But the Student Handbook asks us to forget about all these. It aims at eliminating our differences and ensuring conformity in the school.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: We have found some pamphlets with poems from the outside world printed on them.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: This is something we've never been taught in class ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That poem inspired me with so many things ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We are the chosen ones. We are meant to be the backbone of the primary defense for mankind.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But all of you here today ... Must still be curious about who you really are and what is in the world outside ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We cannot leave here, but we can know the truth through another way.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Fellow students, before entering the school ... Where did you live? What kind of life did you lead?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did people there cast incantations too? Did they like scone just as we do ...?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: By piecing together our memories from all over the world, we can "rebuild" the very world outside!

items.speaker: All Students
items.text: Wow!

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: So that's how you know the world ...!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: This is the safest method we can think of. Given that none of us are leaving the school ...

items.speaker: Student C
items.text: I-I tucked some of these pamphlets in my pocket! And the stained glass balls an instructor left to me when he resigned!

items.speaker: Student C
items.text: I'd say these are a part of the outside world!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Shh, silence! No one speaks before Matilda!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: My name is Matilda Bouanich! I am the most senior transfer student in the school—in fact, I was too senior to be taken in, if not for that special approval. That is to say, I remember the outside world a lot more than you do ...

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: I-I'm Isabella. I was taken here at four, so I don't remember much of the outside world ...

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Hmm, I can recall Mother Superior used to like wearing floral dresses in pale blue, and ...

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: We don't have much rain from where I grew up. The cloudless sky stretched out over our head and fell into the horizon ...

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Our family has been psychologists for generations in the arcanum world. "Animal Magnetism" was invented by my grandfather's grandfather's grandfather's ... grandfather.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But I'm not interested in arcanists. They are all mad people, and we had to treat them after all ... They looked scary.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Oh and, there was a big football field near my house. Bare spots were on the turf everywhere, and there was also rust on the goals ...

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Slow down, SLOW DOWN! What's football? And goal? I can't follow ...!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: The Ring takes down everything. The paper beneath his pen has been densely packed with words, and the note goes on for pages.
Everyone is trying hard to recall the days before coming to school. They feel warm and even united.
They've never been so united before. They have different pasts, but now face the same fate. These experiences make them who they are.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: ... This is a beautiful poem.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Isabella mutters at the pamphlet.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: I want to sing it!

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: She suddenly stands up, which startles the group.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Sing it? How?

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: To the melody of our school song!

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: See, each word is well-matched to the rhythm!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text:
Nor happiness, nor harmony, nor fame,
Nor pride, nor strength, nor skill in arms or arts ... ♪

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: ... My, they do go well together!

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Shepherd those herds whom blindness makes tame ... ♪

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Their eyes see not one light of Bright Stars ... ♪

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: They all stood up with excitement.

items.speaker: Student C
items.text: God, each syllable is joining the notes so well …

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Is this a sign revealed by destiny? Are we told to, told to ...

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: To sing it at the Parade Ceremony!

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Impossible! We will definitely get caught!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: But in doing so, the Big Head will hear our voices!

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: They will come to realize that we ... we have this wish ...

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: They will understand us, won't they, Vertin? After all, it is they who brought us up and who cared for us!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They may be upset, or blame us ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But, let's give it a try!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: In the darkness, their hands join in silence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The song ... sounds much better than it was before.
TO BE CONTINUED…
George the Oak
A wrinkled note is passing in the class.
It begins its journey from the second-to-last row, and soon visits every seat in the classroom.
It doesn't have a particular destination. The next student is where it would go to.
On the back of it says, "Open it."

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Umm ... Okay.
After reading it, Isabella folds the note, with an odd look on her face. She passes it to the student sitting next to her.

items.speaker: Student B
items.text: For whom?

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Hmm ... for you ...

items.speaker: Student B
items.text: From whom?

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: No idea, quit asking! Just open it and pass it down ...

items.speaker: Student B
items.text: *tut* If you do this to waste my time taking notes, I will ...
He unfolds the note. His face suddenly goes pale.
There's only one sentence on the note, written in a crooked font.
"If ur also curious abt the world outside—9 tonight under George the Oak."

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: Hey! Vertin!

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: Did you write this note?

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: He waves his fist; a note is in his grasp. Two more students come up to Vertin.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. Are you coming?

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: Ha ... No.

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: You are gonna shine my shoes for the rest of the week.
Why would I do that?

branch.speaker: Joseph
branch.text: Why? Because of this nonsense you wrote ...!

branch.speaker: Joseph
branch.text: Seems like you need another lesson in the guardhouse, huh?

branch.speaker: Joseph
branch.text: I have the accusation AND the evidence. Surely you don't want one of the instructors to have it, right?

items.text: Why, did you step on something?

branch.speaker: Joseph
branch.text: Damn it ... No! Don't you change the subject!

branch.speaker: Joseph
branch.text: Not only did you pass notes in class, but also did so to spread such ... such horrifying information ...!

branch.speaker: Joseph
branch.text: Ha, you don't want this to be given to the instructors, do you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So that's what you mean ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't care, Joseph. You can deal with it as you want.

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: Come on, cut the crap! Shine my shoes for a week or cry in the guardhouse again!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm messing with you. How would you prove that I wrote it?

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: You ...!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's not what my writing looks like when I use my right hand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And now you are the one holding the note—I could say it's you who wrote it, right?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll call the instructor over for you.

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: You jerk ...! Err-ah!

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: Joseph's face and ears get red. He jumps on Vertin at full strength ...

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: You freak, you're just a bastard that can't even cast an incantation!

items.speaker: Joseph
items.text: Go on, you two! I want her legs broken today!
Escape Plan
George the Oak
The passage of time has done little to change the face of the old oak. Years pass by as fleeting moments but it remains as it ever was.
And just as ever, a flock of little white doves gathers beneath its ancient boughs.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Are you sure this is going to work, Lucas?
A short boy crawls across the ground. He seems to be searching for something.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: You CAN leave if you don't trust me.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Hmph!

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: The school anthem's over. Mikey said he would sneak out when the choir was leaving the stage.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Then, it's time for the principal to give that same old speech that goes on and on. So, let's say 15 minutes, but we might need more time than that. Do you think we can make it?
Lucas stands up and brushes the dirt from his palms.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: C'mon Emilia, don't sweat it! You know the old man'll keep blabbing on for at least half an hour.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: We've still got plenty of time. Just think about it: once the summoning array's done, the three of us will be free.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: I mean out-of-the-school free.
The little girl tenses visibly.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Out of the school, really?

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Do you know what it's like out there? The instructor said there's a war going on. It could be dangerous.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Are you kidding? They just said that to scare us.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: But why are we doing it today of all days?

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Because it's our last good chance for the whole semester. Everyone's at the ceremony, and the guards are busy either handling the crowds or showing the Inspection Team around. I heard there are some Committee members coming this time.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: So, will you calm down already? This was your plan, remember? Everything's gonna go just fine.
Emilia—the planner between them—says nothing. She turns her head to look up at George the Oak.
The grandfatherly tree has nothing to offer but stern and noble silence.
Year after year, new cohorts gather beneath his bright, green leaves as they wither and dry, until they're plucked from his head by the wind, and become the soft mulch on which the new class treads.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Someone's coming.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Could be Mikey. I'll go get him.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Wait. Let me double-check. My arcane skill isn't totally reliable.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Let me see. They sound like a girl's footsteps, a bit shorter than Mikey.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Wait. Now I hear two of them coming this way. Is there something wrong with my arcane skill?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Got you!
The star investigator herself pops out from the bushes.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Shoot! It's a monitor assistant.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Merel, are you in position?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'm ready.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Ah, run!

items.speaker: All Students
items.text: The instructor is here! The instructor is here! Stop fighting!

items.speaker: All Students
items.text: Children scatter and run away.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *coughs* ... I need to hide quickly ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's an empty classroom right next to her. A good place to hide.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The clamor subsides. The hallway restores its peace gradually.
TO BE CONTINUED…
No match for the alumni, the two young students are soon caught and detained beneath the oak tree.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Another two overconfident truants. This happens every year.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Fortunately, your little accomplice in the choir was exposed; otherwise, you would be running free outside the school right now.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Urgh, you're a big jerk!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Wh-What? Don't you realize you could have wound up in danger if the kindhearted and brilliant Matilda hadn't stopped you?
Merel rises to her feet to examine their array, and a peculiar expression crosses her face.
Hapless, yet knowing, like a chef realizing too late what their recipe needed.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You know, this array wouldn't have worked anyway.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: What? Liar! I found it in a book. It said it could summon a gryphon.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Uhhh, Avian Critter Behaviors and Feeding Methods?

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: What? How did you know?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You found this array on the blank page between chapter three and four, right? Drawn in invisible ink.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: "Whosoever unlocks the secret hidden in invisible ink will discover an array which summons the legendary gryphon."
The young boy's eyes go wide as he realizes just how far out of his depth he is.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: You've read that book too, haven't you? And you found this array?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: That's right.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: You mean you went to this school?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Of course. What are you trying to say, exactly?

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Then, you mean we really do get to go back into the world?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: We couldn't stay here even if we wanted to.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: The instructors are hiding something. But if we'll find out one day anyway, why don't they just tell us now?

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Miss, why can't you just tell us what's happening out there? I swear we'll keep our mouths shut.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Don't bother, Emilia. They're not gonna tell you anything.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: They know. But even if they used to be students like us, they're just like them now.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: They'll ignore us, just like the instructors do.
Her face flushes. Terrible secrets threaten to burst from her lips.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: War ... There's a war raging out there. Honestly, I wish I could stay here at the school where it's safe. And that's not even the worst part.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: That must be them. This way. Hurry up!
An instructor arrives flanked by school security guards, disrupting their increasingly dangerous conversation.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Lucas, Emilia! What do you think you're doing out here? Unbelievable!

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: You're both spending the rest of the day sitting in the guardhouse! Take them away!

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: No, no! There's worms in the walls of that place.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Exactly! Those Shamirs are there to give you troublemakers a lesson.

items.speaker: School Security
items.text: Move it, you little terrors. No more tricks. I'm watching you.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Let me go!
The flustered instructor regains her composure and offers the Security Assistance Team a polite smile.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Thank you for your assistance, investigators. Rest assured, I'll be giving these two a much overdue lesson on following rules and procedures.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: You are most welcome, Instructor. Of course, we could escort them to the guardhouse if you'd like.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: No need for that. I'm aware you have more important tasks to do while "the skies are clear."
She seizes the little doves by their wings and escorts them back to the safety of their cage.
Matilda and Merel stay in place, exchanging a look of resigned acceptance, powerless to change things as they are now.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: These students are too young to handle the truth. They don't even know they're from different eras. Could you imagine what would happen if we told them about the "Storm"?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I do understand. I mean, I know the school's only trying to protect them, but their punishment still seems a bit much.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Mhm. Which is why I, the Great Matilda Bouanich, will be changing things as soon as I gain power in the Foundation!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: But for now, let's keep our eyes on the mission, alright? There's no time to wait for Sonetto and Vertin.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: The nearest watchtower is the one in the northwest. Let's start from there.
Top Floor, Northwestern Watchtower

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: So, this is the Shelter Dove.
Merel stands beside the blast door, looking frozen stiff from head to toe.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What are you doing standing back there? Come on, I'll show you how to use the tester.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: What? I thought you said you never used it before.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Perhaps not, but you underestimate Matilda the Magnificent! I already figured out how to use it well in advance.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Oh, okay.
Her stiff posture finally breaks as she walks over to accept the tester from Matilda.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Plug the tester in at the panel on the pedestal, turn the safety knob, and press the button on the side.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The safety knob ... Am I turning it the right way?
A slight buzz emerges from the device.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Okay. Now the lights on the panel will tell us whether the Dove is working.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Verifying ID, green. Power status, green. Immunity area, also green. Good. Stellar. Superb!
She withdraws the tester with satisfaction.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: That's all there is to it. Now we head to the next watchtower.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: By the way, I'm quite curious: how did you know the gryphon array wouldn't work?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Because I was the one who drew it, back in eighth grade.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah, uh, what? But, but, but that's, that's vandalism!
Hallway, St. Pavlov Foundation
The long corridor is like a riddle whose end connects to its beginning. It loops around the Committee Building, linking various floors and rooms with meticulously designed stairways.
Somewhere within that winding riddle, Sonetto comes to a halt.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is there something wrong, Sonetto?
The soft words sound louder and sharper in the empty hallway. The bustle of the Foundation's Pre-Storm activity hasn't yet reached this corridor.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That courtroom we just passed—Mr. Creius is in there answering the Committee's questions.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It was his information that led us to the Amber Room and to Bereggrad. I'm just concerned ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Foundation hasn't quizzed me on anything since I submitted my report on the Don Operation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I would be in there right next to Creius if they wanted to investigate us as well.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I see.
Sonetto suppresses her concerns. Footsteps echo over the marble again.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Here it is. Let's go.
Foundation Office
The office behind the opening door is barren of any identity, a symptom both of the occupant's recent arrival and her curious nature.
The woman in question lifts her head from the neat stacks of files on her desk.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Long time no see, Timekeeper, Sonetto.
The three scuffle, pushing and shoving, but none yields to the others.
The school bell rings. They freeze momentarily. Then, they scatter like kittens and race back to the classroom.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: ...As for the glavakus, they are a kind of critter that primarily inhabits the tropical rainforests of North America.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Being omnivorous, they are an adaptable species with a remarkable ability to form colonies even in the most extreme conditions.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Please turn to page 126 of “The Compendium of Critters.”

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: As you can see, studies show that their colonies operate under a distinct hierarchy.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: The stronger the scent of a glavakus, the higher its status. They rely on their acute sense of smell and sensitive hearing, for they lack vision.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: From our last class, how should you react when encountering such creatures?

items.speaker: Students
items.text: Do not run or jump; walk quietly!
During the students' unified chant, a slight discord can be heard.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Pfft, pfft...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: You two... have truly impressed me. I challenge you to a duel!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: The loser will bow to the winner and become their faithful sailor!
Erick’s assertive voice pierces the chorus, and the instructor frowns.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Erick, you seem to have some... unique opinions.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Stand up and share them.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: W-What?
She stands up hastily. The blackboard reads, “Large, Dangerous Critters.”

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Um...

Clearly, our hero's attention was never on the instructor.
Scratching her cheek, she tries to recall any relevant information.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Well, my grandfather Harald once said...
She looks up at the frowning instructor. The classroom falls silent. All eyes are on her.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: He said, “In life, one must defeat many things, like super-heavy cars or giant brown bears. But the most dangerous of all…

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: “Is the endless Vanity and boundless Emptiness.”
The instructor's eyes flicker with confusion, but she listens intently.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: The monster known as “Vanity” is a huge, winding snake, as large as a mountain range! It opens its mouth, bottomless, and swallows anyone who strays into it.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: It swallows them whole, then spits out the bones in piles a mountain high!
The students gaze unblinkingly, hearts lodged in their throats.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: The monster known as “Emptiness” is a cunning, deceitful creature. One that no one has ever truly seen...!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: It lurks in the shadows. At night, the noises under the bed, the flash outside the window, the drips in the bathroom—any one of them could be it!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Sometimes, it's right next to your ear; at others, it’s far, far away.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: It stalks grown-ups, not with a gaping jaw but with claws as sharp as potato wedges...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: It silently approaches those drowning in sadness, regret, and despair. When they cover their faces, too overwhelmed to be wary, it extends its bloodied claws...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Shwoop!
The students shudder in unison.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: To finish off those poor souls!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: In my view, these are the largest and most deadly of critters.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Of course, I've never met these terrible beasts. Harald says I'm not tall enough yet. But one day, one day, I will.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: I'll knock them down and beat them so hard they can't even stand up straight!
The students' eyes sparkle with admiration, and they quickly break into applause.
Even her opponents, Sancho and Eifer, can't help but get lost in thought.
The instructor sighs. This student will be a bone to chew for sure.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Erick, a fitting critter ought to be...
The ring of the school bell cuts her off. Class is dismissed.
The students swarm, flocking towards Erick.

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Erick, come to my office later.
In the bustling crowd, Erick raises her hand and waves.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Yes, ma'am!
Students' hostel
The night casts its shadows on Erick’s youthful cheeks. She breathes softly.
She lies on her bed, underneath which sits “The History of Potions.” She twirls her pen in her hand.
After a moment, she stops, buries her head in the paper before her, and begins to write.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "Dear Harald—"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "This is my first winter at the SPDM."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "I've met many new sailors here, each boasting their own impressive tricks."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "One can make saplings sprout out of stones; another can fly with the wind; there’s even one who can foresee test questions!"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "My fleet has grown much larger, and there are many places here that I can’t wait to explore."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "I will unearth all the treasures I can here, hide them in my drawer, and give some of them to you when you come to pick me up."
She looks up, glancing at the book on the desk, her brows furrowed.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "But the instructors here are mean. They’re always frowning, and they like locking students up in the guardhouse."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "Today, I spoke of the monsters ‘Vanity’ and ‘Emptiness’ in class."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "The instructor called me to the office and said, 'Those are not considered monsters.' — Can you believe it!?"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "Then she rambled on about the history of critter surveys and made me memorize it all."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "In terms of boredom, these instructors are all the same!"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "Of course, my sailor crewmates support me. They said those were the scariest monsters they'd ever heard of, a hundred times more dangerous than anything in the ‘Critter Dictionary!’ When I walked out of the office, wow—"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "They surrounded me, chanting 'Erick', 'Erick', 'Erick'! I'd never seen such a large and enthusiastic crew!"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "I talked to them from school dismissal till evening. By the end of it, I could hardly feel my tongue!"

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "...But I really miss you, Harald."
She stretches out her hand and rubs her eye.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "When I walked out of the office, for a brief moment, I was expecting to see you standing by the door. Once I’m done with this adventure, be sure to come pick me up in old John's beat-up car."
The sound of footsteps echoes from under the door.
Pfft, pfft!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Oh, right on time...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text:
"Tonight’s duel challengers are here; I have to go.
"Please say hi to old John and his beat-up car for me."

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: "—Your brave and fearless Erick."
She folds the letter, slipping it into an envelope.
Then puts it carefully under her pillow, like a treasure.
George the Oak

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Huff, huff, huff...
Erick pants, hands on the ground, beads of sweat dripping from her golden hair and onto her forehead.
Sancho and Eifer are standing upright, unflinching.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: I thought you were something special... Can't even perform a decent Arcane Skill! Your test scores must be terrible.

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: ...Go back to sleep, dueling her is pointless, she’s no chance of beating us.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Not true! If I could take off this arm ring, you two would be running scared!

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Yeah, right, you people always have excuses –– stomach ache, hungry, rainy weather...

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Always concocting a reason for your failures, then making another grand promise before the end of the week!

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: It’s like running in circles. More pointless than playing catch with a ball...
Footsteps and dim lights approach from the dark road yonder.
Hey, you shouldn’t be out here. What are you doing!?

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Oh no, it's the school disciplinary witch... Run!
But by now, the figure is standing right in front of them. She grabs Eifer and Sancho by their collars.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hah! As the SPDM's disciplinary assistant, leaving without permission—

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh, ow!
Sancho bites the witch’s left arm, giving him a moment to escape her grasp.

items.speaker: The "Great" Storyteller
items.text: Erick lunges at her other arm...
The witch shakes her arm, releasing Eifer, and then—

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text:
Hmph! Caught you! 
You know it's past curfew...
Erick is pinned to the ground, as if weighed down by a pile of stones.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Now's your chance. Run, you idiots!
The two snap out of it and run into the darkness.

items.speaker: The "Great" Storyteller
items.text: They look back, catching a glimpse of our hero’s brave resistance.

items.speaker: The "Great" Storyteller
items.text: Until their vision is obscured by the night's mist...
It didn’t take long for punishment to arrive.
The corridor is empty and silent. Having been punished, Erick stands alone by the classroom door. Her stomach growls.
She glances at her shoes, idly picks her nose, and stares out the window at the dimming twilight. The orange afterglow has reached her knees.
There’s a sudden rustling sound from around the corner.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: A jarl never ever gets scared! Come out now! I mean— you’d better show yourself, or else...
From the corner of the hallway, two little heads pop out like rabbits.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Are you okay?
Erick’s bravely puffed chest finally deflates.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: I snuck you some fried cod... You must be starving.
She grabs the offered meal, devouring it like a bear starved through the winter.

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: ...Why did you help us?

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: (Munching) Because I can't let my future crew fall into another’s hands. It was nothing, really. Being a jarl means more than just giving orders; you have to take on responsibility too.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Even the most powerful of jarls will eventually fall from grace if they avoid their personal responsibilities and simply order others around.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho & Effie
items.text: ...Wow!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: I heard that in ancient times, there was a king who ruled over the biggest forest in the world...
Listening intently, Sancho and Eifer gradually lower themselves to the floor until they are fully seated, utterly mesmerized by her vivid storytelling.
From the fading rays of the twilight sun to the silvery glow of moonlight, night gracefully arrives.
Their eyes glow brightly. They swallow hard, absorbing the tales of greatness, wonder, and the incredible.
TO BE CONTINUED…
